d_preserved_statement: The reviewed mechanic (t1-check-in-per-group, design review r2 PASS 88) is preserved exactly: for each of 3 groups (花組/月組/星組, matching design-sim.mjs's GROUP_NAMES exactly), the child must open both the size/proposed-room card and the per-member allergy card (disclosure gate enforced via `allRead`), then commit ONE room-sufficiency verdict and the exact SET of members needing 個別対応食 (matching design-sim.mjs's `groupWin`/`sessionWin` byte-for-byte) in a single per-group commit (no retry). Gate H and Gate G are both implemented as in implementation_v1.

repair_v2_impl_review_r1_findings_addres.IMPLEMENTATION_FLOW_DIVERGENCE (HIGH): v1 was a single-group wizard (one `index`-based card, silently advancing to the next group on commit with no shown result), diverging from game_spec_v1.json's initial_visual_state ('3枚の班カード（固定表示...それぞれ現在の状態を示すアイコン付き）'). Rewrote HotelReceiveGame.tsx: groupUI is now `Record<GroupId, GroupUI>` (openCards/acceptRoom/specialMealMembers/committed/win, independently tracked per group), rendered via a single `order.map((id) => {...})` pass over all 3 GROUP_IDS simultaneously. Each group has its own disclosure gates and commit button; committing one group immediately collapses that group's card to a locked read-only result summary (完了/まだチェックインできない) while the other groups remain independently interactive -- browser-verified end to end (see implementation_qa_v2.json).
repair_v2_impl_review_r1_findings_addres.STALE_OLD_MECHANIC_CONTENT (HIGH): Two staleness bugs missed in the v1 content pass: (a) schoolTrip.ts's lensSummary.rows entry for the hotel role still said '部屋・食事・入浴の受け入れ' -- fixed to '部屋の確認とアレルギー対応'. (b) hotel-trip experience's place.image still pointed at T('school-trip-hotel') despite art_brief_v1.json's own reasoning that this image should not be reused -- the art_brief decision had never actually been propagated into content data; fixed by removing place.image entirely (place.image is optional per Q1Experience.place in src/data/types.ts, precedented by shopOpening.ts's image-less place entries). gameplay-qa-hotel-receive.mjs strengthened to scan schoolTrip.ts directly (not just the component) for both stale-content patterns.

Reverted hotelReceiveLogic.ts to hoshi/星組/🌟 exactly, matching the approved design chain -- judged lower-risk than retroactively updating 6 already-PASSED design JSON files for a purely cosmetic, zero-gameplay-impact rename (this was also the reviewer's own first-listed recommended remediation).
repair_v2_impl_review_r1_findings_addres.QA_REGRESSIONS_OVERCLAIM_COVERAGE (MEDIU: v1's QA harness claimed to verify 'immediate resolution' but only grepped for setResults/groupWin substrings, not actual UI behavior, and never scanned schoolTrip.ts. gameplay-qa-hotel-receive.mjs rewritten: now asserts the committed-group branch renders the locked summary text but NOT the interactive commit button or dx-more disclosure buttons (proving no retry path), asserts all-3-cards-simultaneous via a unique-occurrence regex count on `order.map((id) => {` (the explicit-block-body pattern unique to the playing view), and scans schoolTrip.ts directly for both STALE_OLD_MECHANIC_CONTENT patterns. 36/36 checks now pass (up from 29 in v1, 2 new checks added).

unrelated_bug_found_and_fixed_during_rep: While browser-verifying the rewritten component, discovered that toggleCard/toggleMember read `groupUI[id]` from the render-scope closure rather than the functional setGroupUI updater's `prev` argument. Under React 18 automatic batching, multiple synchronous clicks in the same event-loop tick (e.g. a script clicking several member checkboxes back-to-back) each computed their 'next' Set from the SAME stale groupUI snapshot, so only the last click's toggle survived -- silently dropping all but one of several rapid selections. This is a genuine implementation bug distinct from the previously-documented browser-automation click-loop artifact (that artifact is DOM-read timing noise with no state loss; this was real React state loss). Fixed both functions to use setGroupUI((prev) => ...) reading prev[id] instead of the closed-over groupUI[id]. Re-verified: the same rapid multi-click sequence that previously dropped 4 of 5 selections now correctly registers all 5.
